title: Fake Merc Character Study (part. 16): Law of Attraction
summary: Part 16 of NH's mocking series on fitness YouTuber Jason Blaha, about Blaha's claims of success with women. NH says Blaha uses fake female accounts to praise himself, and he presents messages that he and others collected over months with catfish accounts on a Facebook powerlifting group. Almost no training content, apart from dismissing Blaha's claim that women don't care about looks.
claims: NH says he teased the message revelations a month early to provoke Blaha; the reaction (fake accounts, deleted messages) helped him confirm which accounts were Blaha's
He says he cross-checks every claim in the series several times, because attacking a liar means he can't lie himself
NH says Blaha posted a video arguing rows are good for novices the day after NH's anti-row video
Pickup artists are clueless about women; taking dating advice from them makes no sense
Against the claim that women don't care about physique, NH says women are highly receptive to looks, roughly as much as men
NH puts his own female audience at about 1-2%, which he says is already high for fitness YouTube
NH says he and others spent about six months on catfish accounts in a Facebook powerlifting group to collect Blaha's messages to women
He calls advice to narrow-stance squatters to bend over and use the lower back more a recipe for injury
